title: GS Caltex runs children's ecology drawing class at Seoul Forest learning garden - 헤럴드경제
content: Coloring program and drawing contest set for Sept. 5 GS Caltex announced Monday it is running a "Children's Ecology Observation Drawing Class" for children and families at the Seoul Forest learning garden, which is hosting the 2026 Seoul International Garden Expo. Registration is available on-site at the learning garden or through the Seoul Green Trust website. The program was designed to give residents a hands-on experience of the Seoul Forest learning garden, which was renovated in April. GS Caltex originally supported the creation of the space when Seoul Forest opened in 2005, and has since transformed it into a learning garden where visitors can explore and learn about nature through a range of ecology programs. By closely observing and sketching plants and insects, children can deepen their understanding of ecosystems and discover the beauty of the natural world. GS Caltex is also running a coloring program using the garden's ecological resources, and plans to hold a coloring session and an ecology observation drawing contest at the Seoul Forest learning garden on Saturday. "We hope children will learn about the beauty of nature and the value of biodiversity through the process of directly observing and recording plants and insects," a GS Caltex official said. "We look forward to the learning garden becoming an environmental education space where citizens can learn about and document nature." Meanwhile, GS Caltex continues to carry out a range of corporate social responsibility initiatives beyond operating the Seoul Forest learning garden, spanning environmental education and carbon reduction. These include planting salt marsh vegetation to build blue carbon reserves, coastal cleanup activities, and energy efficiency improvement projects.

title: Estimated 2027 GS Pay Scale - FedSmith.com
content: The estimated 2027 GS base pay table is based on President Trump's alternative pay plan for federal employees. President Trump’s 2027 alternative pay plan letter issued on August 26, 2026, recommended freezing the General Schedule (GS) pay scale for 2027, leaving base pay and locality pay unchanged from 2026 rates for most federal civilian employees. However, the letter also authorizes a separate 3.8% pay increase for federal law enforcement personnel. The letter follows through on the White House’s 2027 budget proposal, which did not include a civilian pay raise. Congress has not passed legislation setting a different 2027 pay adjustment, and the freeze won’t be official until Trump signs an executive order in December which is the step that actually locks in next year’s pay tables. This estimated 2027 GS base pay table carries over the 2026 figures without change, since the alternative pay plan sets 2027 base pay at 2026 rates. FedSmith will update this table if the final 2027 pay rates differ from these figures. Because the alternative pay plan sets 2027 locality pay at 2026 levels, these are the presumed amounts for 2027, unchanged from their current amounts. No new locality pay areas or boundary changes are expected for 2027. The Federal Salary Council had recommended new standalone localities for the Kennewick-Richland-Walla Walla, Washington, and Syracuse-Auburn, New York, areas, along with boundary expansions in Ohio and Arizona. The President’s Pay Agent rejected those recommendations in its December 2025 annual report, stating it would not approve further additions to existing locality pay areas or the creation of new ones “at this time.” Yes. Separate from the civilian pay freeze, the alternative pay plan letter directs the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to use its special rate authority to give certain law enforcement personnel a 3.8% pay raise next year. Trump used the same approach for the 2026 federal pay raise, when OPM published special rate tables covering GS-1 through GS-15 in early January after determining eligible categories over the preceding months. Because the LEO raise is implemented through OPM’s special rate authority rather than through the General Schedule, the GS pay tables elsewhere in this article do not reflect the 3.8% increase. OPM has not yet announced which law enforcement categories will qualify for the 2027 increase. FedSmith will provide updates as they become available. FedSmith has compiled estimated 2027 LEO pay tables by applying a 3.8% increase to the 2026 LEO locality pay tables published by OPM. These are estimates and may not match the final figures implemented by OPM when the 2027 LEO pay raise is finalized. FedSmith will update this article with new information as it becomes available, including when the final 2027 pay figures are released. title: Karol G’s ‘BbY WOW’ Lyrics & English Translation: What Song Does It Sample? - justjared.com
content: The 35-year-old Colombian superstar’s “BbY WOW” with Judeline and Rusowsky, featured on her new album NO ME ARREPIENTO DE SENTIR TANTO, is steadily surging up the streaming charts, and fans are eagerly looking up the lyrics and English translation, as well as the familiar song it samples. As of the end of August, the song broke through the Billboard Hot 100 to No. 38, and is already a No. 1 hit on US Hot Latin Songs and Hot Latin Rhythm Songs charts. Karol broke down the story behind the song in an in-depth interview for Rolling Stone. I felt like I needed a song, one that people could dance to in the club but that also had that emotion. So, what happens when you’re in the club and you’re heartbroken? You just think about the other person, about the song you’d love to be dancing to with that person. The first version of the song was just me. But I felt like, live, I wanted to sing that song with more people on stage and for it to really become a bit more of a party. And that’s when I thought of Rusowsky and I said to Judeline, “Why don’t you join the song?” I worked a lot on that album with Judeline because the way she sings about love made me feel how men sometimes don’t understand how deep a woman’s pain can be. She has something special, and it’s that every emotion feels so intense. She has a song called “Is God Good or Just Powerful?” It’s literally one that lasts about a minute and a half. What she sings is super short, it’s like a verse and a chorus. And I was like, “Wow, how can you say so much in a verse and a chorus?” So it was literally a must for me to write music with her for this album. Our teams got in touch. We told her I was making new music and she traveled to Los Angeles. I spent about a week with her, and it was really nice because the first thing we did was sit down and talk, like, “I’ll give you some context about where I am, how I’m feeling.”We were both going through almost the same thing, so I loved that because we were in sync and it just worked. I thought, “We’re both here, feeling almost the same thing, it’s going to flow in a special way.”We were in the studio for about three or four days, and we made more music there that isn’t on the album. The song samples the “Coolie Dance” riddim by Cordell ‘Scatta’ Burrell and Everton, as popularized on “Move Ya Body,” the 2004 hit by Nina Sky featuring Jabba and Kat DeLuna‘s “Whine Up,” among other hits over the years. title: Vikings Mourn Death of Former QB & Punter Bob Lee - Minnesota Vikings
content: EAGAN, Minn. — The Vikings are mourning the loss of former quarterback and punter Bob Lee, who passed away Aug. 17, just 10 days after he turned 81. Lee holds the distinction of punting in Minnesota's first Super Bowl appearance (IV) and throwing the most recent touchdown by a Viking in a Super Bowl (XI), a 13-yarder caught by Stu Voigt in the fourth quarter against the Raiders. He made the Vikings roster in 1969 and played in the NFL through 1980, totaling 77 regular-season games played for Minnesota, Atlanta and the Los Angeles Rams. In 30 starts at quarterback, Lee posted a 19-11 record with the Vikings. He played in eight postseason games, making three starts. That's pretty impressive, considering he entered the NFL as a 17th-round pick (441st overall out of 462 picks) out of the University of the Pacific in 1968. Lee made his pro debut in the 1969 season opener, punting six times in a game at the Giants in which Fran Tarkenton led New York to a comeback win against his previous and future team. The following week, after Joe Kapp tied an NFL record with seven touchdown passes against the Baltimore Colts, Lee attempted his first pro passes, going 4-for-6 with 35 yards in the 52-14 Vikings win. Lee first met Kapp (with Vikings 1967-69) long before they became teammates. In fall 2019 both were among attendees during a 50th anniversary celebration of the 1969 NFL Champions. The reunion included panel discussions, during which Lee shared his memory of meeting Kapp the first time when Kapp was QB at Cal and Lee was 12. "I met Joe Kapp when I was 12 years old and he was a junior at the University of California on a 1-9 team," Lee explained. "My dad ran The Associated Press in San Francisco. They were in competition with other wire services. They hired a college senior journalism student to do the postgame stories. Those stories for the Eastern papers paid a nickel a word. They were 1,500 words, so 75 bucks, which was a big deal in 1957. "The senior didn't show up. They said, 'The press pass works. Go down there, write a bunch of notes. We'll turn it into a story.' The first guy I listened to was Joe Kapp," Lee continued. "Joe took all the blame for the loss. Nobody else. It was his fault. … He was a leader. He didn't push himself in certain directions on other people." Lee attempted one pass in a 51-3 win over Cleveland on Nov. 9, 1969, and went 3-for-4 with his first touchdown, a 7-yard strike to John Henderson in a 52-14 win over the Steelers two weeks later. During the 1969 postseason, Lee punted three times in a 23-20 win over the Rams and thrice more in a 27-7 victory over the Browns, helping Minnesota advance to Super Bowl IV. He punted three times in that game as well. After making two starts as a backup late in 1970 but not punting that season, he returned to those duties in 1971. Lee made four starts in the regular season, as well as the playoff game against Dallas in the Divisional Round. Lee also handled punting duties in that loss to the Cowboys. That was the final time he punted in an NFL game. Tarkenton's return to Minnesota in 1972 led to Lee returning to a reserve QB role before he was traded to Atlanta in 1973, when he posted his best results, going 8-2 for the Falcons. After one more season there, he returned to Minnesota in 1975. Lee backed up Tarkenton over the next four seasons and went 4-1 in five starts from 1976-77. "Bob Lee was under appreciated at how good he was at quarterback," Tarkenton said. "He was a great backup QB for us and a good starter for the Atlanta Falcons. Plus, Bob was an absolutely great human being that you could depend on anytime. He was as good of a teammate as you could ever have." When Tarkenton suffered a broken leg in mid-November of the 1977 season, Lee won three of four starts to help Minnesota finish 9-5. Playing through a broken right hand during the stretch, he then quarterbacked the Vikings to a win over the Rams in the Divisional Round of the NFC Playoffs, a game that came to be known as the "Mud Bowl." "Playing on a field like this is worse than snow," Lee said after the game. "You're slipping, your runners are slipping and your receivers are slipping. I think the thing that I was most impressed by was the way our ball carriers and receivers held onto the ball. It's kind of amazing that we didn't have one turnover." Rams QB Pat Haden threw interceptions to Nate Allen, Paul Krause and Jeff Wright. The Cowboys, however, prevailed over the Vikings in the NFC Championship Game on the way to a convincing win in Super Bowl XII. Lee capped his career with two seasons as a backup with the Rams. His final scoring pass was a 41-yarder against the Vikings in a pivotal 27-21 overtime win for L.A. From 1991-96 Lee proudly served as director of athletics at University of the Pacific, helping expand the school's athletics and fitness facilities. He became one of 22 charter members in the Pacific Athletics Hall of Fame in 1982. Other roles Lee held including serving on the board of directors for the Northern California chapter of the National Football Foundation and Hall of Fame, as well as chairman of the San Francisco Special Olympics in 1981. © 2026 Minnesota Vikings Football, LLC , All Rights Reserved.

title: BMW R 1300 GS: The Adventure Bike That Eliminates The Need For A Second Motorcycle - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update Owning multiple motorcycles sounds like the dream. You have one for weekday commuting, another for weekend canyon roads, and a third to disappear into the wilderness. Reality, however, slaps you in the face and reminds you that more motorcycles mean higher insurance costs, more maintenance, and more garage space. That's why many riders don't look for a bike that satisfies just one purpose, but one that handles a wide variety of rides. Motorcycles capable of handling nearly every situation have become more desirable over the years, and adventure bikes are leading that charge. A one-bike garage is simple. You don’t divide riding time between specialized machines. Instead, with every passing mile, you build familiarity with a single motorcycle. You learn its strengths, understand its personality, and develop your confidence in your skills, regardless of whether the road ahead looks freshly paved or covered in loose gravel. Adventure motorcycles have become the biggest reason why single-bike ownership is a realistic option. They combine upright ergonomics, long-travel suspension, generous luggage options, and capable engines, allowing riders to travel wherever they choose, be it their workplace or a remote village few others have visited. ADVs have steadily evolved into some of the most versatile machines on the market. While early generations leaned heavily toward either off-road exploration or long-distance touring, today’s flagship bikes are engineered to do both exceptionally well. They get large fuel capacities, advanced electronics, adaptive suspension, sophisticated rider aids, and increasingly refined engines. Riders today don't even have to choose between highway comfort and off-road capability, because most modern ADVs are designed to deliver both in the same package. Now, if you are looking for something that balances everything perfectly, there is exactly one bike for it. Need to commute? The bike feels manageable despite its size. Planning a thousand-mile road trip? This is built for exactly that. Curious about what’s at the end of a dirt track? Long-travel suspension and enduro equipment to the rescue. For decades, the BMW GS family has become the benchmark against which nearly every large ADV is measured. The R 1300 GS continues that legacy while introducing one of the most comprehensive redesigns the model has ever received. Compared with the previous R 1250 GS, almost every major component has been reworked. There is a new steel sheet-metal main frame, a die-cast aluminum rear frame, a more compact boxer engine, lower overall weight, updated suspension, and significantly expanded electronic capabilities. BMW also focused heavily on improving everyday usability. The lower center of gravity thanks to the boxer engine contributes to low-speed balance, while an optional automated transmission and adaptive ride height reduce intimidation for shorter riders. The result is an adventure bike that appeals equally to world travelers and daily commuters alike. At the heart of the BMW R 1300 GS sits a 1,300 cc air/liquid-cooled flat twin engine (best known as a boxer twin) that churns out 145 horsepower at 7,750 rpm and 110 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 rpm. This makes it one of the most powerful production boxer engines BMW has ever installed in one of its motorcycles. The best part? Despite the increased output and capacity, the engine is actually more compact than before. BMW repositioned the transmission beneath the engine while redesigning the overall layout to save space and reduce weight. Now, the engine’s personality changes dramatically depending on how the motorcycle is configured. Power delivery is broad, but the ride modes allow the rider to adjust throttle response and traction to their particular use case. There is an ECO mode that incorporates BMW's ShiftCam technology. This varies valve timing and valve lift to improve fuel economy as well as power delivery on long stretches of highway. The R 1300 GS also comes with a six-speed gearbox as standard. However, optionally, you can ask for the Automated Shift Assistant. This allows for fully automatic shifting or manual operation without a conventional clutch lever. A welcome feature when you consider what a burden stop-and-go traffic can be on the daily commute. The R 1300 GS represents one of the most comprehensive redesigns in the model's history. BMW replaced the tubular steel frame with an entirely new steel sheet-metal main frame for increased rigidity and tighter packaging size. The rear, too, has a new die-cast aluminum lattice rear frame. This is suspended on BMW's signature EVO Telelever front suspension and EVO Paralever rear suspension, while braking is handled by two 310 mm discs at the front with four-piston radial calipers, and a single 285 mm disc at the rear clamped by a two-piston floating caliper. Now, suspension technology has become one of the biggest advantages of premium adventure motorcycles, and the R 1300 GS pushes that even further. BMW’s Dynamic Suspension Adjustment continuously adapts damping characteristics according to riding conditions, throttle inputs, speed, and road surface. This is optional, but combined with the adaptive vehicle height features, it makes low-speed maneuvers, starts and stops, and parking considerably easier, even with a full load of luggage strapped to the bike. Although completely redesigned, the BMW R 1300 GS remains instantly recognizable as a GS. The signature boxer engine continues to define its silhouette, and the bodywork is noticeably more compact, improving both balance and reach to the ground. Ergonomics place the rider in a commanding upright position, giving them excellent control and reduced fatigue during long journeys. You also get multiple seat heights, adjustable ergonomics, luggage systems, and comfort packages to tailor the bike for touring, off-road expeditions, or even everyday riding. The R 1300 GS showcases just how sophisticated adventure motorcycles have become. A full-color TFT display provides navigation, smartphone connectivity, riding data, and vehicle information. LED lighting comes standard, while an optional adaptive headlight actively follows the motorcycle through corners. Radar-based Riding Assistant tech introduces active cruise control, front collision warning, lane change warning, and rear-end collision warning. Keyless ride, heated grips, tire pressure monitoring, hill start control, engine drag torque control, and numerous other electronic rider aids round out an already extensive suite of technology.​​​​​​​ Replacing multiple motorcycles is an ambitious goal, but the BMW R 1300 GS comes remarkably close. It possesses enough comfort for long-distance touring, enough performance to satisfy spirited road riding, enough capability for genuine off-road exploration, and enough practicality to function as everyday transportation. The search for the perfect all-around motorcycle has always been difficult, but the GS blends those qualities more effectively than most of its rivals. We want to hear from you. title: Vikings at Broncos Game Observations - Minnesota Vikings
content:
DENVER — The Vikings preseason wrapped Friday night with Carson Wentz starting at quarterback and playing two series before handing the reins of Minnesota's offense to Max Brosmer. Minnesota Head Coach Kevin O'Connell and Denver Head Coach Sean Payton opted to rest starters on both sides of the ball in the 34-6 Broncos win. O'Connell had hoped J.J. McCarthy was able to recover from an ankle injury suffered on a hit the previous week against the Baltimore Ravens. McCarthy was limited in practice early in the week and did not participate at all Wednesday in a practice that had more of a scrimmage format. Wentz finished 3-for-4 passing with 15 yards and a passer rating of 80.2. His longest completion was a gain of 6 to tight end Gavin Bartholomew. Brosmer opened by hitting his first few short completions and drove the Vikings 55-yards into the red zone late in the second quarter before the drive stalled in the red zone. Will Reichard booted a 28-yard field goal to cap the drive that lasted 4:00. The only problem was Denver stormed right back by driving 65 yards in just 1:08 thanks to Sam Ehlinger going 4-for-5 and accounting for all 65 yards through the air. Jaleel McLaughlin capped the drive with a 20-yard catch-and-run touchdown, securing the grab on the right side and showing his speed as he zoomed to the left. Brosmer finished 20-of-35 passing with 166 yards and a passer rating of 69.5 Ehlinger finished 15-for-20 with 233 yards and three scores. His passer rating was 131.9. View game action photos from the Vikings preseason game vs. the Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High. Undrafted rookie Jacob Thomas had really been making the most of his opportunities and started on Friday along with third-round pick Jakobe Thomas, who made his pro debut after missing Minnesota's first two preseason contests because of back tightness. Jacob Thomas unfortunately suffered an injury while defending a pass on the seventh play of the game. He was slow to get up after landing out of bounds. It was a tough end to a preseason that had started with such promise for Thomas, who recorded an interception at New York in his NFL debut. Jacob Thomas was replaced by Kahlef Hailassie, who recorded an interception in the second quarter to set up Minnesota's first score. Linebacker Jacob Roberts, who had recorded Minnesota's other interception against the Giants, also left the game with an injury. One of the battles that hadn't yielded much indication is at punter where veteran Johnny Hekker and undrafted rookie Brett Thorson. It likely wasn't going to be decided by Friday's action alone, which is good because the stats were about as even as possible. Thorson punted three times for 156 yards for an average of 52.0 and with a long of 58. Hekker? Three punts for 156 yards and an average of 52.0 with a long of 57. Times inside the 20-yard line? Twice each for both players. Ehlinger enjoyed a fourth quarter for the ages. He was able to orchestrate a 17-play 85 yard drive that lasted 9:58 and concluded with a 14-yard touchdown pass to Cody Schrader on fourth-and-2 with 13:04 remaining. Ehlinger also capitalized on a busted coverage that left rookie tight end Justin Joly completely uncovered in the middle of the field. Joly was able to catch it and run for an 88-yard score to cap a 93-yard drive that lasted just three plays and 1:39. The Broncos racked up 412 yards by going 7-for-14 on third downs and averaged 6.4 yards per play. Denver went 2-for-3 on fourth downs. Minnesota was unable to push the ball down the field much and finished with 270 yards. The Vikings went 3-for-13 on third downs and averaged 4.7 yards per play. The Vikings concluded the season with just one touchdown across three games (a fade from Wentz to Myles Price at New York). Minnesota went 0-for-2 on trips inside Denver's 20-yard line. title: BMW Motorrad International GS Trophy Namibia Recap - Video - Yahoo Sports
content: Ahead of the BMW Motorrad International GS Trophy 2026 taking place in Romania, we thought we'd take a look back at our time alongside Team USA during the 2024 event in Namibia. To recap, 22 teams – 16 men's, and 6 women's – arrived in Windhoek to compete against each other and the unforgiving terrain of the African continent. Though some of the landscape was similar to the American Southwest, coming around a corner to a herd of giraffes, wildebeest or oryx quickly reminded one that they were not in Kansas (North Carolina, Texas, or Florida) anymore. Representing Team USA was Kirk Graydon from South Carolina, Billy De Wet from Texas via South Africa, and Scott Acheson from Florida. Regrettably, the American women's qualifying team was unable to advance past the semi-final rounds during this year's competition. For this event, the teams would be competing on the then-new BMW R 1300 GS, BMW's flagship adventure machine which received a massive update for the model year. With the event in its ninth edition, we'd span 1,300 km, competing and building lasting friendships with riders from all over the world as the team took on the daily challenges and battled the Namibian outback. It truly was a once in a lifetime experience that the competitors will hold with them forever. For 2026, GS Trophy contenders will compete in the wilds of Romania where dense forests, intense elevation changes, and river crossings will surely test each rider's mettle as they take on the challenge. For equipment, BMW's retro-scrambler, the R 12 G/S gets the full Trophy treatment, adding a touch of nostalgia to the event while offering real adventure capability. Hopefully this video recap can serve as an appetizer for the 2026 GS Trophy. To the competitors, good luck and soak up every moment of the journey. title: No 2027 Federal Pay Raise: Freeze Base and Locality Pay at 2026 Rates - MyFederalRetirement

Financial Planning Resources for Federal & Postal Employees President Trump has formally frozen federal civilian pay for 2027, transmitting his alternative pay plan letter to Congress on August 26. The letter proposes holding both base pay and locality pay at 2026 rates for most federal employees, while authorizing a 3.8% increase for law enforcement personnel and raises of 5% to 7% for military members, depending on rank. Congress can still override the freeze, but has not done so in similar years past, and the alternative pay plan typically becomes final when OPM issues the official 2027 pay tables in December. If it stands, 2027 would be the smallest civilian pay adjustment since the freeze years of the early 2010s. Enter your email  on this form [CLICK HERE] (opens in new tab)and we’ll send you an email alert as soon as the 2027 pay raise (or freeze) is finalized — plus what it means for your specific grade and step. The letter cites(opens in new tab) the Federal Employees Pay Comparability Act (FEPCA), which requires the president to submit an alternative pay plan each year by August 31 or allow a statutory formula to take effect automatically. According to the letter, that formula would have triggered locality pay increases averaging 20.6% at a cost of $26 billion in the first year, on top of a 3.1% across-the-board base pay increase. The administration says freezing pay avoids that cost. OPM has not yet said which categories of law enforcement personnel will qualify for the 3.8% increase; that determination is expected to follow the same process used for the 2026 raise. These two figures get confused every year, and this year is no different. The federal pay raise applies only to current employees and is set through the political process described above. The COLA applies to retirees and is calculated automatically from the Consumer Price Index, with no input from the president or Congress. The 2027 COLA will be announced in October once third-quarter CPI-W data are final, with early estimates pointing to a range of roughly 3.5% to 3.7%. If you’re within a few years of retiring, a frozen salary year does more than just hold your paycheck flat. It also affects your High-3 salary average, since that figure is built from your highest 36 consecutive months of basic pay. A year with no raise pulls that average down slightly compared to a year where pay kept rising, and the effect compounds if your final year of service happens to fall during the freeze. Here’s a simplified illustration. Assume a FERS employee earning $114,000, with 2% annual raises in a normal year, compared to the same employee whose final year is frozen at 0%. In this example, the frozen year lowers the High-3 average by about $775. Multiplied by your years of service and pension multiplier, that’s a modest but real reduction to your annuity for the rest of your retirement. It’s not large enough to change most people’s retirement plans on its own, but it’s worth factoring in if you’re deciding between retiring at year-end versus waiting for a possible raise, or if you’re already running the numbers on when to file. A frozen across-the-board and locality rate doesn’t mean your paycheck is completely stuck. Within-grade step increases still apply on their normal schedule if you’re not already at the top step, and any promotion or locality area change still raises your pay. Those factors can offset some or all of the freeze’s effect on your High-3, depending on where you are in your career. Congress has until the alternative pay plan takes effect to pass legislation setting a different number, most likely through the FAIR Act, which would provide a 4.1% raise. That bill has been introduced every year since 2014 and has never passed. Barring a change, OPM will issue the final 2027 pay tables in December, and the freeze outlined in this letter will take effect on the first pay period of January 2027. Gold is projected to extend its recent gains in the second half of 2026, even as growing use of some derivatives tied to the metal could be making gold prices more volatile, according to Goldman Sachs Research. Goldman Sachs Research forecasts the precious metal will rise to $4,900 per troy ounce by the end of the year. Gold rallied 15% from its mid-July low to around $4,600 per troy ounce as of August 25. The metal is expected to rise as central banks continue diversifying their reserves and markets scale back expectations for US rate hikes in 2026. Demand for gold from central banks is a key structural factor underpinning the metal’s rally, according to Lina Thomas, senior commodities analyst in Goldman Sachs Research, and Daan Struyven, co-head of Global Commodities Research. “We continue to see elevated central bank gold accumulation as a multi-year trend, as central banks diversify their reserves to hedge geopolitical and financial risks, consistent with recent survey evidence,” Thomas and Struyven write. Central banks have been diversifying their holdings using gold, which is considered less likely to be frozen than reserves held in foreign currencies. They have been buying gold at an increased rate since 2022, when G7 countries responded to the invasion of Ukraine by freezing Russian central bank assets in Europe. Goldman Sachs Research expects central banks to buy an average of 50 tonnes of gold per month in 2026, up from an average of 17 tonnes per month before 2022. Central bank purchases accelerated to 100 tonnes per month in June 2026 (on a three-month seasonally adjusted basis) from 66 tonnes the previous month, according to Goldman Sachs Research’s nowcast of central bank activity. China’s central bank was the largest identifiable buyer in the market in June. Interest rate expectations are another important factor supporting recent gold price increases. Demand from some investors is starting to recover from a slow first half of the year as markets scale back expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in 2026. Historically, gold tends to struggle when interest rates rise, as higher rates reduce the appeal of gold relative to yielding assets like bonds. “We expect the Fed-related headwind to abate further, as our economists expect a lower inflation trend to keep the Fed on hold this year,” Thomas and Struyven write. The researchers also highlight a range of medium-term factors that could cause the gold price to exceed Goldman Sachs Research’s forecast for 2026. “Gold’s share in private portfolios remains low, and recent geopolitical developments—including Iran and broader tensions—may accelerate diversification beyond central banks to private investors, including by weighing on perceptions of Western fiscal sustainability.” Demand for gold call options is rising as investors turn to the instruments to hedge their portfolios against large-scale changes in government policies. This has the potential to amplify price swings in both directions, Thomas and Struyven explain. As gold rises, it is approaching key strike levels for some call options, forcing options dealers that sold these calls to buy gold in order to hedge their short exposure to the metal, accelerating the rally. On the other hand, declines in the gold price could prompt dealers to reverse those hedges by selling their gold holdings, driving prices even lower. Goldman Sachs Research’s forecast for gold to reach $4,900 per troy ounce by the end of 2026 does not incorporate elevated demand for hedges through gold derivatives. This could increase the likelihood that the gold price exceeds the forecast, but it also suggests “greater two-sided volatility” to the gold rally, Thomas and Struyven write. Energy markets have been surprisingly resilient amid the disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. However, there are few signs of relief in markets for refined products such as diesel, gasoline, and jet fuel, says Nitin Jindal, head of Global Commodities in Goldman Sachs FICC and Equities, on The Markets podcast. Jindal also discusses China’s remarkable adjustment to the disruption in energy supplies and the outlook for natural gas prices in Europe as winter approaches. Chris Hussey: This is The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey, and today is Wednesday, August 26th, and we're here on the Goldman Sachs trading floor with Nitin Jindal, who heads up our global commodities business within global banking and markets. Nitin, thanks so much for joining us on The Markets. Chris Hussey: Okay. I want to start with a breaking point question because we're about to celebrate, celebrate is not the right word, the sixth straight month of the Strait of Hormuz being closed. Has it surprised you that this has not disrupted the commodity markets more, or do you think we really are at a breaking point? Nitin Jindal: Several things have surprised me, right? First, just the length of the war. That's surprising. But it shouldn't be surprising given what is happening in Europe, where we have-- we are at a four-and-a-half-year point, and nobody would have ever predicted at any point that that conflict would go this long. The other thing which is very surprising is how resilient the market has been in terms of finding supplies and not actually breaking down. Nitin Jindal: There are several things which have- which were done, several protective measures which were taken. Still, have a major, epically major disruption in the market, and prices are, you know, within a tolerable range. Chris Hussey: Okay, let me explore this one element around inventories. Cause some of the pictures I've been seeing lately is oil inventories are coming down now, and they're down to levels where we haven't seen them normally. Does that get you concerned that we're going into a place where we just have no more oil to give back and we're finally going to get that breaking point? Nitin Jindal: If you'd have asked me that question two months ago, my answer would have been absolutely yes. We were heading into the highest demand window, which is typically summer. Now we are kind of getting out of the demand window, and we were fine in the summer window. So especially for crude oil, I don't think we'll break in next few months. Products might be a different story. We have a very tight products market. The refining complex stays tight. We are getting less product out of Persian Gulf. We're getting less product out of Russia due to attacks on Russian refining by Ukraine. We're not getting products out of China due to just preservation. So the world ex-Persian Gulf, ex-Russia, ex-China is tight products, and there is no immediate release valve which is coming. Having said that, prices are already high, so what we like is we like the roll-up, which exists in the market, specially in crack spread space. Chris Hussey: Let me explore China for a little bit, if we can, because China has been an area which has had some demand destruction to help out with everything that's taking place. Can we see any more demand destruction out of China, or is that all we got? Nitin Jindal: It's highly unpredictable. Six months ago, nobody could have predicted that China could adjust by that, that much amount. But now that we, we have seen it, let's look at the hard data which makes it happen. China sells 34 million cars a year right now, so their fleet is growing rapidly, but a lot of it is EV. They can, hence they can switch from gas to electric easy. Their electricity sector is also growing rapidly. Last year, they installed 500 gigawatts of new capacity, mostly solar, some wind, some batteries, some gas. To put it in perspective, US only installed 50 gigs. And hence, they have no shortage of electricity. They can easily switch if needed without using more hydrocarbons. I would be surprised they can do a lot more, but I would also not be shocked if they did more Chris Hussey: Okay. So, one last commodity I wanted to talk about was nat gas, because there's a commodity that's more to do with Europe maybe than China, but China needs nat gas. If they can't get it from the Middle East, they might take it from the US, and then not enough gets to Europe. How much trouble will Europe get in if the Strait of Hormuz isn't reopened here and they can't get the LNG out to the right spots? Nitin Jindal: In the short term, it really depends on what happens this winter weather, right? Like, you must have also heard this term El Niño. El Niños are warm. So if you have a warm, if you have this El Niño which turns out to be very warm, you know, the world is going to get bailed out because the swing in gas demand due to weather is so strong that you can easily manage the supply disruption. And if you go past this season, there was so much oversupply coming from like US, Australia, that you could see a balanced market. Now, that's only true if you get a very, very warm winter. If you get a normal winter, you have a very tight setup going into this winter. If you get a normal winter, China will literally need to back off because Europe would then compete. And Europe would not just compete for gas. Europe would compete for gas and coal. Both very important fuels for China. Now, the flip side to that is that China itself produces about 30 BCF a day of natural gas. They have been growing their production. So, if you look at last year or so, China has stopped taking more LNG than what they used to historically take. Can they actually adjust that down by 20%? Probably, but that's not enough to offset the supply loss we have from Qatar. Chris Hussey: Yeah, I guess the ironic good news here is there's a super El Niño taking place here, which suggests normal weather might be less likely than normal. Chris Hussey: Okay. Put a bow on all this. What's the trade? Nitin Jindal: We like being long crack spreads, right? Specifically, term like Cal 27 cracks are not, you know, pricing continued disruption. We like being long Asian hydrocarbons versus US hydrocarbons. We think the freight market is tight. It will continue to stay tight. Look, if you look at, you know, Panama Canal is very tight right now. You cannot simply relieve all these supply chain logistics quickly. So, but when you again look at the forward freight market, it's not fully pricing all these dislocations. We like gold as a debasement trade. We like US nat gas as well going into this winter. Again, assuming normal-ish winter. So those are big themes like. We like US power market on the AI theme. Chris Hussey: Okay. What are you looking for in the, uh, couple of weeks ahead here? Nitin Jindal: You know, bring the summer to an end. Looking back, for kids to go to school. And I have a trip coming up in Europe next month. Chris Hussey: All right, great. And hopefully, in the middle of all that, you'll be able to watch a little cricket and see if India can beat Sri Lanka. Nitin Jindal: Well, I'll let you know tomorrow. Thank you so much. Chris Hussey: Thanks so much. That does it for this week's episode of The Markets. I'm Chris Hussey. Thanks for listening. title: BMW R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition Marks a Brazilian Milestone - stupidDOPE
content: A factory anniversary can easily become an exercise in commemorative badges and ceremonial paint. BMW Motorrad has taken a more considered route in Brazil, using the R 1300 GS Adventure to connect a decade of motorcycle production in Manaus with a significant manufacturing milestone. The resulting BMW R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition is limited to just ten motorcycles, one representing each year of operation at the Brazilian facility. The choice of model carries particular weight. The R 1300 GS Adventure was also the 150,000th motorcycle produced at the Manaus plant, making the flagship adventure bike more than a convenient platform for a special edition. It represents both the scale BMW’s Brazilian operation has reached and the increasingly international manufacturing footprint behind one of motorcycling‘s most recognizable nameplates. Each anniversary motorcycle receives a deep olive-drab finish accented by yellow pinstriping and exclusive graphics across the fuel tank, side panels, and top case. An Akrapovič dual slip-on exhaust adds another distinguishing element, while BMW’s Automated Shift Assistant introduces a more consequential technological feature. The 1,300cc boxer engine remains mechanically unchanged, producing a claimed 145 horsepower and 110 pound-feet of torque. For a motorcycle already positioned near the top of BMW’s adventure range, the significance of this edition comes less from additional performance than from context. It connects an important motorcycle, a manufacturing landmark, and BMW Motorrad’s decade-long presence in Manaus through a production run small enough to function almost as a set of rolling historical markers. The tenth anniversary matters because BMW’s Manaus operation represents more than an assembly point serving a regional market. Reaching 150,000 motorcycles demonstrates sustained production at a meaningful scale, and selecting the R 1300 GS Adventure as the milestone machine connects that industrial achievement to one of BMW Motorrad’s most globally recognizable products. Brazil presents compelling reasons for localized motorcycle production. It is one of the world’s substantial motorcycle markets, with two-wheel transportation serving roles ranging from daily mobility to recreation and premium touring. Manaus, meanwhile, has long been an important manufacturing center through the Manaus Free Trade Zone, where industrial policy has encouraged domestic production across numerous sectors. BMW Motorrad’s presence there places the German company’s engineering culture within a distinctly Brazilian manufacturing context. That matters because modern premium vehicles are increasingly international products even when their brand identities remain closely tied to their countries of origin. The R 1300 GS Adventure captures that reality particularly well. Its engineering lineage is unmistakably BMW, from the boxer engine architecture to the chassis philosophy and electronics surrounding it. Yet this particular group of motorcycles also represents ten years of Brazilian production capability. The anniversary edition consequently commemorates people and infrastructure as much as machinery. Limited-edition motorcycles are common, but the logic behind their production numbers can sometimes feel arbitrary. A run of 500 or 1,000 examples creates scarcity, yet the number itself rarely contributes much to the story. BMW’s decision to produce ten examples is considerably more direct. One motorcycle represents each year of operation at the Manaus factory. That makes the limited quantity part of the commemorative concept rather than simply a mechanism for creating exclusivity. Numbering each example strengthens that connection. These motorcycles are not merely R 1300 GS Adventures equipped with an unusual paint package. Each occupies a specific place within a deliberately tiny production series linked to the facility’s history. That distinction will likely matter most over time. Special-edition motorcycles frequently become more interesting as the events they commemorate move further into the past. Production anniversaries, engineering transitions, final editions, competition victories, and factory milestones provide collectors with historical reference points that ordinary colorways cannot. The Manaus edition has two such anchors: the factory’s tenth anniversary and its 150,000th motorcycle. The deep olive-drab finish is particularly appropriate for the R 1300 GS Adventure. Adventure motorcycles already borrow some of their visual identity from expedition equipment. Large fuel tanks, exposed structural components, protective hardware, luggage systems, tall suspension, substantial windscreens, and upright ergonomics communicate purpose before the engine is even started. Olive drab pushes those associations toward military and field equipment without turning the motorcycle into a literal historical reference. Yellow pinstriping provides the necessary counterpoint. Against the muted bodywork, the brighter linework emphasizes the shape of the motorcycle while preventing the finish from becoming visually flat. Exclusive graphics across the tank and side panels establish the anniversary identity, while extending the treatment to the top case makes the luggage feel integrated into the design rather than attached afterward. Cases and other touring equipment occupy significant visual space, and mismatched accessories can disrupt an otherwise carefully developed design. Treating the top case as part of the commemorative package reinforces the sense that the edition was conceived as a complete motorcycle. The palette also avoids one of the more common problems with anniversary products: excessive decoration. BMW does not need gold surfaces, oversized dates, or elaborate graphics to communicate significance. The restrained finish suits a machine whose reputation was built around capability. The GS name carries unusual weight within BMW Motorrad. BMW’s adventure-bike lineage stretches back decades, and the GS family helped establish the template for large-displacement adventure motorcycles long before the segment became one of the industry’s most competitive categories. The formula combined long-distance road ability with off-pavement capability, upright ergonomics, luggage capacity, and the company’s horizontally opposed boxer engine. Modern GS models have become considerably more sophisticated, but that central proposition remains recognizable. The R 1300 GS generation represents a substantial evolution of the formula. Its 1,300cc boxer engine delivers 145 horsepower and 110 pound-feet of torque, output substantial enough to handle highway touring, luggage, passengers, steep grades, and off-road situations where careful throttle control becomes more important than outright power. The Adventure version expands the platform’s long-distance intent. That makes it particularly fitting as a factory milestone. A 150,000th motorcycle could have been almost any model on the production schedule. Having the number land on the R 1300 GS Adventure gives BMW a machine capable of representing the breadth of its modern engineering approach. It is technologically sophisticated, historically recognizable, and built for the kind of large-scale travel with which the GS identity has become synonymous. BMW has resisted the temptation to increase engine output simply to distinguish the anniversary edition. The familiar 1,300cc boxer remains rated at 145 horsepower and 110 pound-feet of torque. Special editions do not automatically become better when manufacturers increase power. On a large adventure motorcycle, additional output can have limited practical value compared with improvements in control, ergonomics, suspension behavior, heat management, reliability, or rider assistance. The existing engine already provides considerable performance. More importantly, the horizontally opposed twin remains fundamental to the GS experience. Its low-mounted cylinders contribute to the motorcycle’s recognizable silhouette while helping position substantial engine mass lower in the chassis. Decades of development have transformed the boxer from a historical curiosity into a highly sophisticated modern powerplant. Leaving it mechanically intact keeps the anniversary edition connected to the standard motorcycle rather than creating an unnecessarily altered derivative. BMW’s Automated Shift Assistant is arguably the anniversary edition’s most consequential equipment feature. The system replaces conventional manual clutch operation with electronic actuators capable of managing clutch and gear changes. Riders can retain control over shifting when desired or allow the motorcycle to handle gear selection automatically. That creates an interesting evolution for a category traditionally associated with mechanical rider involvement. Manual transmissions have long been treated as an essential part of motorcycling because clutch and gear selection contribute directly to the physical relationship between rider and machine. Automation inevitably raises questions about whether convenience removes part of that connection. BMW’s approach is more nuanced because it preserves choice. A rider can still select gears manually without managing a traditional clutch lever, while automatic operation becomes available when circumstances make it preferable. Heavy traffic, extended touring, fatigue, or repetitive low-speed riding can all make reduced clutch work attractive. Adventure motorcycles present a particularly interesting use case because their operating environments vary so dramatically. A rider might spend hours covering highway distance, navigate stop-and-go city traffic, climb winding mountain roads, and eventually encounter loose surfaces or technical terrain. A transmission system capable of changing behavior across those situations has legitimate value. Rather than simply making the R 1300 GS Adventure easier, the technology attempts to make it more adaptable. The Akrapovič dual slip-on exhaust provides a more traditional premium upgrade. Akrapovič has become deeply established within high-end motorcycle culture, with its exhaust systems appearing across everything from road-going sport bikes to racing machinery and adventure motorcycles. The brand’s reputation comes from a combination of materials expertise, weight reduction, acoustic tuning, performance development, and manufacturing quality. On the anniversary R 1300 GS Adventure, the dual slip-on configuration provides a visible distinction from standard equipment while complementing the motorcycle’s premium positioning. The exhaust also introduces another sensory element. Motorcycles are experienced through sound and vibration as much as visual design. An exhaust system can change the character of an otherwise familiar powertrain without requiring fundamental engine modifications. That makes the Akrapovič system a logical addition to a commemorative model whose engine output remains standard. It adds personality without disrupting the proven mechanical foundation. The R 1300 GS Adventure also illustrates how dramatically the adventure category has evolved. Early adventure motorcycles were comparatively simple machines whose appeal came partly from mechanical straightforwardness. Modern flagship ADV bikes increasingly resemble technological showcases, incorporating sophisticated electronics, electronically managed suspension, advanced braking systems, selectable riding modes, navigation integration, radar-based assistance on some models, and increasingly automated drivetrain functions. This evolution reflects what riders ask these motorcycles to do. A modern adventure bike may serve as a commuter, interstate touring machine, weekend canyon motorcycle, two-up traveler, gravel-road explorer, and long-distance expedition platform. That breadth requires compromises, but it also rewards adaptable technology. BMW’s Automated Shift Assistant belongs within that trajectory. Purists may prefer complete manual control, and simpler motorcycles retain advantages in cost, weight, familiarity, and field serviceability. Yet the growth of electronic assistance does not necessarily contradict adventure riding. Technology can reduce workload during mundane sections and preserve rider attention for situations that demand it. The anniversary edition therefore represents more than ten years of factory production. It also captures where the GS concept has arrived technologically. Perhaps the most interesting aspect of the R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition is the geography behind it. BMW remains inseparable from German engineering culture, yet the Manaus edition demonstrates how international the production of premium vehicles has become. Manufacturing expertise does not remain confined to the location where a brand was founded. A Brazilian-built anniversary GS makes that reality visible. For the Manaus workforce, the 150,000-unit milestone represents accumulated manufacturing experience. For BMW, it demonstrates the ability to maintain a premium product identity across an international production network. For collectors, the ten motorcycles connect those industrial circumstances to a physical object. That gives the edition a kind of authenticity that cannot be created solely through cosmetic customization. The olive-drab paint, yellow pinstriping, numbered production, exclusive graphics, Akrapovič exhaust, and Automated Shift Assistant all contribute to desirability. Yet the motorcycle’s real distinction comes from what it represents. The best commemorative vehicles make their special status easy to explain decades later. The BMW R 1300 GS Adventure 10th Anniversary Edition already has that advantage. It celebrates ten years of production at BMW’s Manaus factory, arrives as a ten-unit numbered series, and uses the same model that became the facility’s 150,000th motorcycle. Its specifications reinforce the story without overwhelming it. The deep olive-drab finish and yellow pinstriping establish a distinct visual identity. The Akrapovič dual slip-on exhaust gives the motorcycle an appropriate premium hardware upgrade. Automated Shift Assistant demonstrates where BMW’s touring technology is heading. Meanwhile, the unchanged 145-horsepower boxer preserves the mechanical character of the underlying R 1300 GS Adventure. That balance is important. Anniversary models often become collections of options assembled around a commemorative badge. This edition has a clearer reason to exist because the motorcycle itself is directly tied to the event being celebrated. Only ten examples ensure that relatively few riders will ever own one, but scarcity is not the most interesting part of the project. The Manaus edition captures a specific moment in BMW Motorrad’s manufacturing history while demonstrating how far the GS has evolved from its comparatively elemental adventure-bike origins. title: Owner Raises $240M Led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives to Build the AI-Native Platform for Every Local Business - PR Newswire

Existing investors Meritech, Redpoint, Headline, and Jack Altman also participated. Owner is the AI CMO and CTO for local businesses. It builds and runs their technology and marketing. That includes their websites, online ordering, mobile apps, CRM, customer support, POS, and AI phone ordering. Its AI agents manage and improve each part automatically. Big corporations spend billions on tech and marketing. Small businesses can't afford that, so Owner is building AI to do that work for them. Owner launched in 2020 and has surpassed $100 million in ARR. This year alone, independent restaurant owners will drive more than $1 billion in sales through Owner. Thousands of local businesses use the platform, more than 100 million American consumers have used it, and it now powers more U.S. locations than Domino's or Taco Bell. Owner is the #1 rated restaurant technology on Capterra and G2. A local business owner can talk to Owner like a member of the team. Owner's agents build and run the business's digital presence 24/7. They learn what works across thousands of restaurants and improve performance automatically. A business can ask Owner to promote a menu item, and its agents can create the promotion, update the website, build the campaign, generate the creative, and publish it. Owner can also answer the phone, take orders, reply to reviews and emails, and support customers. "The world is racing to build AI to replace people's jobs. Owner is building AI to do the opposite: to do the jobs many small business owners have never been able to afford," said Adam Guild, co-founder and CEO of Owner. "Now, for the first time, local restaurants have the same tech advantages as the huge chains they compete with. And soon every small local business, including grocers and salons, will have those advantages too." Owner's team includes leaders from Shopify, DoorDash, Compass, Salesforce, and HubSpot. More than 35 team members are former founders. The company also uses AI throughout development. It builds in weeks or months what once took years. Next, Owner will serve every U.S. independent restaurant, expand internationally, and bring its AI system to every local business: salons, spas, independent grocers, and more. title: SOOSAN INT's eSafe AI V3 Wins Top GS Certification - thelec.net
content: SOOSAN INT's generative artificial intelligence (AI) gateway solution, eSafe AI V3, has received Grade 1 certification under the Good Software (GS) quality certification program. SOOSAN INT said the Grade 1 certification officially validates the software quality and product maturity of eSafe AI V3. The cybersecurity company plans to use the certification to strengthen its push into the enterprise market, including public institutions and the financial, manufacturing and IT sectors, where the use of generative AI is expanding. GS certification is a nationally recognized quality certification that comprehensively evaluates software in areas including functionality, reliability, usability, efficiency, maintainability, portability, performance, interoperability, connectivity and compliance. Certified products are eligible for support in public-sector procurement, including contracts with the Public Procurement Service and registration on the Korea ON-line E-Procurement System, and can receive preferential consideration in public information technology projects. eSafe AI V3 is an integrated generative AI platform tailored to AI environments and a generative AI prompt security solution incorporating data loss prevention (DLP) capabilities. According to SOOSAN INT, the product allows multiple large language model (LLM) platforms to be used and managed through a single interface, while detecting and blocking in real time potential leaks involving prompt inputs, keywords, attachments and personal information. The platform also allows organizations to centrally manage multiple generative AI services, providing visibility into AI use and enabling consistent application of security policies. Organizations can establish security governance policies by setting differentiated access permissions for individual users and departments. The platform also provides real-time analysis of usage, token consumption and costs associated with AI services, and allows administrators to set usage limits.
